outcome: A failed dispatch leaves evidence, not just a fingerprint: the observation a failed attempt was digested from is durably readable - its transport status, duration, diagnostic code, terminal events, and usage - so diagnosing a runner_error means reading the journal, never brute-forcing a digest hunt against bytes the engine threw away.

acceptance.text: Every attempt that completes without a sealed handoff - runner_error, invalid_driver_handoff, operational failure - persists its marshaled observation body durably, associated to the attempt whose observation_digest it matches. Anchor: internal/runtime/dispatch.go:2070-2083, where observationBody has exactly two uses today - digest and drop - and the attempts schema (internal/journal/schema.sql:60-73) holds no body column, so the digest's pre-image exists nowhere in the system. Pinned by journal and dispatch tests covering the runner_error and invalid_driver_handoff branches (dispatch.go:2084-2124).

The persisted body is digest-verified and bounded honestly: reading it back re-verifies against the attempt's observation_digest (the evaluation read path's CORRUPT_JOURNAL posture at internal/journal/evaluation.go:143-146 is the precedent), and if a bound must truncate, the truncation is explicit - a marked partial body, never a silent one; the digest always remains over the full marshaled bytes.

The evidence is reachable without archaeology: a journal read surface returns the failed attempt's observation for a given effect and attempt, and the marshal error silently discarded at dispatch.go:2070 no longer produces a digested-nothing - a failed marshal is itself recorded loudly. Pinned by store API tests.

The journal schema change ships with an honest migration: existing journals open cleanly, their historical failed attempts simply have no stored body, and reads say so distinguishably from corruption.

constraints: Evidence basis (2026-08-22, drive-survival r3): the sonnet verifier's first dispatch runner_error'd twice, ~35-40 minutes each, with identical observation digests and zero readable detail on any durable surface - the diagnosis cost a brute-force digest hunt. This slice is that gap's structural fix.

The observation body is contentless by construction today - driver.Observation's Diagnostic carries a code and byte counts, never stderr content (internal/driver/invoke.go:109-113,124-132) - and persistence must preserve that property: this slice stores what the engine already digests, and any future content-bearing observation field meets the bound and the secret-guard posture at this seam.
The digest stays the identity: stored bytes are evidence for the existing digest, never a second authority; nothing about attempt identity, admission, or retry semantics changes.
Check evidence belongs in the submission's checks field, never in files added to the repository.
Schema migration follows the journal's existing migration discipline (the migrate_v1_to_v2 precedent) and the full unit suite is the compatibility gate.
